climate_pressure: Participants in selected Basse-Casamance communities described irregular rainfall and environmental degradation.
documented_impact: The same participatory study reports food-access difficulties and disrupted agricultural livelihoods.
fcv_mediator: Landmines, fear and displacement restrict access to farmland and production, narrowing livelihood options under environmental stress.
possible_consequence: These constraints can leave climate-sensitive food systems less able to absorb further shocks; the interaction is conditional, not a measured joint causal effect.
alternative_explanations: Poverty, markets, salinization, deforestation and labor constraints can affect food access independently of conflict-climate interaction.
uncertainty: One purposive cross-sectional study combines respondent perceptions with historical context. It does not estimate a climate-conflict interaction, current mine prevalence or a national effect.
resilience_factors: Participants propose reforestation, sustainable farming and stronger environmental governance; their effects were not evaluated.
compact_statement: In selected Casamance communities, mines and displacement restrict farming under environmental stress; a conditional reverse-FCV vulnerability mechanism, not climate-caused violence.
